text:
Alisa: FYI seeing sustained egress TX queue saturation on rack-eu-west-3, started ~09:12 UTC. impacting a handful of model-streams.
Matt: saw higher tail latency for hosted text-gen routes, looks correlated to same timeframe.
devops-bot: alert: NIC_TX_95=92% host=gpu-rack-23-node-7
Renee: tenant-42 is doing large batch exports again, they were supposed to use burst pool. Are they on dedicated slices on this rack?
Alisa: yes, tenant-42 pinned to shards on rack-eu-west-3 for data locality. Their KV cache churn is high and egress bursts spike.
Kai: we could preemptively reseed them to eu-west-3-burst to isolate egress, but need a graceful handshake to avoid model-state loss.
Matt: what's the shortest safe sequence? full drain will cause cache misses and regen cost.
Renee: propose handshake + staged drain:
```
# mark pool draining
redwoodctl pool annotate --pool rack-eu-west-3 --annotation state=draining
# tell routing to prefer fallback for new requests
redwoodctl routing update --tag tenant-42 --prefer eu-west-3-burst
# trigger tenant rehome (staged)
redwoodctl tenant rehome --tenant tenant-42 --strategy staged --batch-size 5
```
Kai: during staged rehome we should snapshot KV and replicate to fallback, then warm cache read-through on a small percentage (5-10%) before shifting traffic.
sre-oncall: i'll run a micro-probe: reroute 1% traffic for 10m and monitor token latency, kv hitrate, and nic_tx.
Alisa: also add a temporary per-tenant egress quota to cap spikes while we move them.
Matt: cost question — what's rough delta if we offload to burst pool that uses cross-az egress? Renee: short estimate ~ $180-300/day for extra egress + compute while caches rebuild. Cheaper than repeated SLO violations.
Kai: we must also update the routing policy to allow fallback model-variants that are quantized; risk: small accuracy regressions; add eval gate for high-value endpoints.
Renee: rolling this during low-traffic window around 02:00 UTC. I'll own the orchestration, Kai you handle KV snapshot/replication, Matt you watch agent metrics, Alisa validate SLO windows.
sre-oncall: started canary at 2359876600, 1% traffic -> rerouted to eu-west-3-burst. monitoring: nic_tx at source host down to 45% after initial handoff, kv hitrate drops 12% for canary group.
Matt: tail latency for canary within 15ms of baseline. no error spikes.
devops-bot: event: rehome-stage-1 completed for 5 shards tenant-42 @2359876620
Renee: proceeding to next batch. will pause if nic_tx rises or error_rate > 0.5%.
Alisa: small note — set routing fallback TTL to 600s so we don't flip-flop during transient spikes.
sre-oncall: all batches complete at 2359876650. final check: rack-eu-west-3 nic_tx_95 now 51%, hosted tail latency recovered.
Matt: nice. estimate cost for this operation ~ $220/day for the remainder of migration.
Renee: creating follow-up GH issue: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/1456 to track automating handshake + egress-cost calc + one-click rehome.
Alisa: thanks team. will document playbook in Runbook repo and add routing-policy guardrails. :thumbsup:
